evidence.quote: § 870.1420 Coronary artery disease risk indicator using acoustic heart signals.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: Classifies coronary artery disease risk indicators using acoustic heart signals as Class II devices subject to special controls on testing, algorithm validation, biocompatibility, software, usability, electrical safety and labeling. Addressed to device makers; the text states no effective date.
summary.long: 21 CFR § 870.1420 defines a coronary artery disease risk indicator using acoustic heart signals as a device that records heart sounds including murmurs and vibrations to calculate a patient-specific risk of presence of coronary artery disease, as an aid in cardiac analysis and diagnosis. Paragraph (b) classifies the device as Class II (special controls) and sets out the special controls: clinical performance testing covering the patient population and representativeness of the intended use population; acoustic performance testing of microphone sensitivity, sound acquisition bandwidth and amplitude accuracy; a scientific justification for the algorithm, including verification and validation on an independent data set; biocompatibility of patient-contacting components; software verification, validation and hazard analysis; human factors and usability testing; electromagnetic compatibility and electrical safety data; and labeling that describes the device outputs, placement instructions, care and cleaning, sensor acquisition warnings and expected performance for all intended use populations and environments. The text contains no effective date, penalty or enforcement provision.
